children.translated_text: 1. Proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>), together with their semblances, are for the understanding of others;

children.text: pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca sābhāsaṃ tv ātmasaṃvide //
children.translated_text: <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), together with their semblances, are for one's own understanding.

body.text: iti śāstrārthasaṃgrahaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the summary of the meaning of the treatise.

body.text: 2. vādinā svayaṃ sādhayitum iṣṭo 'rthaḥ sādhyaḥ / sādhyate yena tat sādhanam /
body.translated_text: 2. The object that the proponent himself wishes to establish is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved). That by which it is proved is the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof).

body.text: 3. hetos trirūpavacanam / kāni punas tāni triṇi rūpāṇi / pakṣe sattvam evety ekaṃ rūpam / sapakṣa eva sattvam iti dvitīyaṃ rūpam / vipakṣe cāsattvam eva niścitam iti tṛtīyam //
body.translated_text: 3. The statement of the triple form (<s>trirūpa</s>) of the <s>hetu</s> (reason). What then are those three forms? Existence in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject) alone is the first form. Existence only in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case) is the second form. Definite non-existence in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case) is the third.

body.text: 4. tatra pakṣaḥ prasiddho dharmī prasiddheṇa viśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sādhayitum iṣṭaḥ pratyakṣādyaviruddhaḥ / yathā śabdo dharmī anityatvena viśeṇa viśiṣtaḥ sādhyate kṛtakatvād iti hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: 4. Therein, the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is a well-known <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor), qualified by a well-known qualifier, which one wishes to establish oneself, and which is not contradicted by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and the rest. For example, the <s>dharmin</s> 'sound' qualified by the qualifier 'non-eternality' is to be proved. 'Because of being produced' is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

body.text: 5. kaḥ sapakṣaḥ / sādhyadharmeṇa sāmānyena samānaḥ sapakṣo yathā ghaṭādir iti //
body.translated_text: 5. What is the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case)? That which is similar through commonality with the <s>sādhya</s> property is the <s>sapakṣa</s>, for example, a pot and the like.

body.text: 6. ko vā hetor vipakṣaḥ / yatra sādhyābhāvena hetor abhāvo niyamena kathyate [ yathākāśādir iti //
body.translated_text: 6. What then is the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case) of the <s>hetu</s> (reason)? That wherein, due to the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, the absence of the <s>hetu</s> is stated with certainty, for example, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like.

body.text: 7. etad eva ca hetos trirūpavacanaṃ parapratyāyanāya prayujyamānaṃ parārtham anumānam ucyate / yathā anityaḥ śabda iti pakṣavacanaṃ kṛtakatvād iti hetuvacanam / ghaṭādivad iti sapakṣavacanaṃ / ākāśavad iti vipakṣavacanam //
body.translated_text: 7. This very statement of the triple form of the <s>hetu</s> (reason), when employed for the purpose of convincing another, is called <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others). For example, 'Sound is non-eternal' is the statement of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). 'Because of being produced' is the statement of the <s>hetu</s> (reason). 'Like a pot and such' is the statement of the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case). 'Like space' is the statement of the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case).

body.text: 8. tat punar dvividhaṃ dṛṣṭam / sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca /
body.translated_text: 8. This is seen to be of two kinds: through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).

body.text: 9. tatra sādharmyeṇa tāvat / yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvam anityaṃ dṛṣṭam / yathā ghaṭādiḥ / kṛtakaś ca śabda iti //
body.translated_text: 9. Of these, through similarity first: Whatever is produced is all seen to be non-eternal, like a pot and such. And sound is produced.

body.text: 10. vaidharmyeṇa punaḥ / asaty anityatve na bhavaty eva kṛtakatvaṃ yathākāśādau / śabdas tu kṛtaka iti //
body.translated_text: 10. Through dissimilarity moreover: In the absence of non-eternality, there is never any being-produced, as in space and such. But sound is produced.

body.text: 11. kaḥ punaḥ pakṣābhāsaḥ / yaḥ pakṣa ivābhāsate / na tu sākṣāt pakṣo bhavati / pratyakṣādibhir bādhitatvāt //
body.translated_text: 11. What then is a <s>pakṣābhāsa</s> (semblance of thesis)? That which appears like a <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) but is not directly a <s>pakṣa</s>, because of being contradicted by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and the rest.

body.text: 12. sa tu pakṣābhāsaḥ / yathā dhūmādir dharmībuddhimatā hetunā janyata iti sādhye / pratyakṣaviruddhaḥ pakṣābhāsaḥ / pratyakṣeṇa vahnijanyasya dhumasya darśanāt //
body.translated_text: 12. That <s>pakṣābhāsa</s>: for example, when the <s>sādhya</s> is 'Smoke and such, as <s>dharmin</s>, is produced by an intelligent cause,' this is a <s>pakṣābhāsa</s> contradicted by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), since the production of smoke from fire is observed through direct perception.

body.text: 13. anumānaviruddho yathā / vedavākyaṃ dharmy apauruṣeyam iti sādhye / prayatnānantarīyakatve śabdasya pauruṣeyatvasya prasādhanāt //
body.translated_text: 13. Contradicted by <s>anumāna</s> (inference), for example: When the <s>sādhya</s> is 'Vedic speech, as <s>dharmin</s>, is non-personal,' since sound's being produced immediately after effort establishes its personal origin.

body.text: 14. svavacanaviruddho yathā / nānumānaṃ pramāṇam iti parapratipādanāya vacanam uccāryamāṇaṃ parārtham anumānam ity uktatvāt //
body.translated_text: 14. Contradicted by one's own statement, for example: 'Inference is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)' — since the utterance spoken for communicating to another is stated to be <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others).

body.text: 15. lokaviruddho yathā / śuci naraśiraḥkapālaṃ prāṇyaṅgatvāc chaṅkhaśuktivat //
body.translated_text: 15. Contradicted by common convention (<s>loka</s>), for example: 'A human skull is pure, because it is a part of a living being, like a conch shell or oyster shell.'

body.text: 16. pratītiviruddho yathā / kiyatkālasthāyī kṛtako 'nitya iti / kiyatkālasthāyino 'pi kṛtakāḥ sarve nityā iti lokapratīteḥ //
body.translated_text: 16. Contradicted by accepted understanding (<s>pratīti</s>), for example: 'What endures for any length of time and is produced is non-eternal.' But according to common worldly understanding, all things that endure for any length of time and are produced are eternal.

body.text: 17. aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇo yathā / vaiśeṣikasya sāṃkhyaṃ prati vināśī śabda iti sādhye //
body.translated_text: 17. With an unestablished qualifier, for example: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s [thesis] to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>: when the <s>sādhya</s> is 'Sound is destructible.'

body.text: 18. aprasiddhaviśeṣyo yathā / sāṃkhyasya bauddhaṃ prati ātmā cetana iti sādhayataḥ //
body.translated_text: 18. With an unestablished qualificand, for example: The <s>Sāṃkhya</s>'s thesis to the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist), establishing 'The self (<s>ātman</s>) is conscious.'

body.text: 19. ubhayāprasiddho yathā / vaiśeṣikasya bauddhaṃ prati
body.translated_text: 19. With both unestablished, for example: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s [thesis] to the <s>Bauddha</s>:

body.text: sukhādi
body.translated_text: pleasure and such

body.text: samavāyikāraṇam ātmeti
body.translated_text: have the self as their <s>samavāyikāraṇa</s> (inherent cause).

body.text: prasiddhasaṃbandho
body.translated_text: With an established relation,

body.text: yathā vāyur asthirasvabhāva iti //
body.translated_text: for example: 'Wind has an unstable nature.'

body.text: 20. uktāḥ pakṣābhāsāḥ // //
body.translated_text: 20. The <s>pakṣābhāsas</s> (semblances of thesis) have been stated.

body.text: 21. hetvābhāsaḥ kīdṛśaḥ / yo hetur ivābhāsate / na punaḥ siddho hetur iti //
body.translated_text: 21. What is a <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (semblance of a reason) like? That which appears like a <s>hetu</s> (reason) but is not an established valid reason.

body.text: 22. hetvābhāso 'siddho viruddho 'naikāntikaś ceti triprakāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 22. The <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (semblance of a reason) is of three types: unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: 23. tatra pakṣe 'siddhatvād asiddhasaṃjñako hetvābhāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: 23. Therein, the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> designated 'unestablished' is so because of not being established in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject).

body.text: 24. pakṣasapakṣayor nāsti / vipakṣa evāsti sa viruddhasaṃjñako hetvābhāsaḥ / sādhyaviparyayasādhanāt //
body.translated_text: 24. That which does not exist in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject) and the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case) but exists only in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case) is the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> designated 'contradictory,' because it establishes the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved).

body.text: 25. tatra yo hetuḥ sapakṣavipakṣayor ubhayatrāsti nāsti vā saṃdihyate / aprasiddhasaṃbandho vā so 'naikāntikasaṃjñako hetvābhāsaḥ / vādinaḥ prativādino vā sādhayitum iṣṭasyaikāntasyāsādhanāt //
body.translated_text: 25. A <s>hetu</s> (reason) that exists or does not exist or is doubtful in both the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s>, or whose connection is unestablished, is the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> designated 'inconclusive' (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because it fails to conclusively establish what is desired to be proved by either proponent or opponent.

body.text: 26. ubhayāsiddhaḥ tadyathā śabdasyānityatve sādhye cākṣuṣatvaṃ hetuḥ vādiprativādinor asiddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 26. Unestablished for both parties, for example: When the non-eternality of sound is to be proved, the <s>hetu</s> 'being visible' is unestablished for both proponent and opponent.

body.text: 27. cetanās tarava iti sādhye sarvatvagapaharaṇe maraṇād iti hetuḥ prativādino bauddhasyāsiddha iti prativādyasiddhaḥ / caitanyādinirodhasya bauddhenopagamāt //
body.translated_text: 27. When the thesis is 'trees are conscious,' the reason 'because complete removal of bark causes death' is unestablished for the Buddhist opponent — this is <s>prativādyasiddha</s> (unestablished for the opponent); because the Buddhist accepts the cessation of consciousness and so forth.

body.text: 28. acetanāḥ sukhādaya iti sādhye / utpattimattvād iti hetuḥ svayaṃ vādinaḥ sāṃkhyasyāsiddhaḥ / iti vādyasiddha iti //
body.translated_text: 28. When the thesis is 'pleasure and so forth are non-conscious,' the reason 'because they possess origination' is unestablished for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> proponent himself — this is <s>vādyasiddha</s> (unestablished for the proponent).

body.text: 29. vaiśeṣikasya bauddhaṃ prati kṣamādikaṃ dharmī kāryam iti sādhayataḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ sadṛśāparāparotpatter iti svayaṃ vādino 'siddhaḥ / utpattau siddhāyām api pratikṣaṇasadṛśāparāparotpattir ity asiddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 29. When the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, proving against the Buddhist that earth and so forth is the subject and 'is an effect' is the thesis, [uses] the reason 'because of the successive origination of similar successors at each moment' — this is unestablished for the proponent himself; even when origination is established, the successive origination of similar successors at each moment is unestablished.

body.text: 30. pakṣaikadeśāsiddho yathā / cetanās taravaḥ svāpād iti hetuḥ / digambarasya svayaṃ vādinaḥ pakṣaikadeśāsiddhaḥ / na hi sarve vṛkṣā rātrau patrasaṃkocabhājaḥ //
body.translated_text: 30. An example of <s>pakṣaikadeśāsiddha</s> (unestablished in part of the thesis) is as follows: The reason 'because of sleep' [to prove] 'trees are conscious' is unestablished for the <s>Digambara</s> proponent himself in part of the thesis; for not all trees exhibit the folding of leaves at night.

body.text: 31. tathā pṛthivyādikaṃ dharmī buddhimaddhetujanyam iti sādhye kāryatvād iti hetur bauddhaṃ praty asiddhaḥ / pratyakṣānupalambhanibandhano hi kāryakāraṇabhāvo bauddhasya pṛthivyādau na siddhaḥ / vihārāhārādiṣu siddhaṃ cet tadā pakṣaikadeśāsiddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 31. Likewise, when earth and so forth is the subject and 'produced from an intelligent cause' is the thesis, the reason 'because of being an effect' is unestablished for the Buddhist opponent; for the cause-effect relationship grounded in <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) is not established for the Buddhist regarding earth and so forth. If [one says] 'it is established in dwellings, food, etc.,' then it is <s>pakṣaikadeśāsiddha</s> (partially unestablished in the thesis).

body.text: 32. saṃdigdhāsiddho yathā yady ayaṃ dhūmo 'gnir atreti sādhye hetor evāniścayāt //
body.translated_text: 32. An example of <s>saṃdigdhāsiddha</s> (doubtfully unestablished): When the thesis is 'if this is smoke, there is fire here,' because of the very uncertainty of the reason.

body.text: 33. dharmisaṃdehe 'py asiddho yathā / iha bahuṣu nikuñjeṣu kvacid ekasmin nikuñje mayūra iti sādhye kekāyikād iti hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: 33. An example of being unestablished due to doubt about the subject: 'In some one grove among these many groves, there is a peacock' — the reason being 'because of the cry.'

body.text: 34. dharmyasiddhāv apy asiddho yathā ātmā dharmī sarvagata iti sādhye sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvād iti hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: 34. An example of being unestablished even when the subject is established: When the subject is the <s>ātman</s> (self) and 'all-pervading' is the thesis, the reason is 'because of qualities being perceived everywhere.'

body.text: 35. daśaite 'siddhasaṃjñakā hetvābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 35. These ten are the <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) designated as <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished).

body.text: 36. // anaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ kīdṛśa ucyate //
body.translated_text: 36. What kind of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reason) is the <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) one? It is stated:

body.text: 37. yathā śabdasya nityatvādike dharme sādhye prameyatvaṃ hetuḥ sapaksvipakṣayoḥ sarvatra vartamānaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ //
body.translated_text: 37. For example, when permanence and so forth of sound is the property to be proved, the reason <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability), being present everywhere in both <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances) and <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances), is a <s>sādhāraṇa anaikāntika</s> (common inconclusive reason).

body.text: 38. tathā śabdasya nityatve śrāvaṇatvaṃ hetuḥ sapakṣavipakṣayor apravartamānāt / asādhāraṇānaikāntikaḥ //
body.translated_text: 38. Likewise, when permanence of sound [is to be proved], the reason 'audibility' — since it does not occur in either <s>sapakṣa</s> or <s>vipakṣa</s> — is an <s>asādhāraṇa anaikāntika</s> (uncommon inconclusive reason).

body.text: 39. tathā śabdasyāprayatnānantarīyakatve sādhye 'nityatvād iti hetuḥ / sapakṣaikadeśavṛttir vipakṣavyāpy anaikāntikaḥ // aprayatnānantarīya

children.text: ḥ śabdasya vidyudākāśādiḥ sapakṣaḥ tatraikadeśe vidyudādau vartate 'nityatvaṃ nākāśādau prayatnāntarīyakaḥ punaḥ sarvo ghaṭādir vipakṣaḥ / tatra sarvatra vartate //
children.translated_text: is lightning, space, etc. Among those, impermanence occurs in part, namely in lightning and so forth, but not in space and so forth. The <s>vipakṣa</s> of what is produced by effort consists of all [things like] pots and so forth; impermanence is present in all of those.

body.translated_text: 39. Likewise, when 'sound is not produced by effort' is the thesis, the reason 'because of being impermanent' occurs in only part of the <s>sapakṣa</s> and pervades the <s>vipakṣa</s>, [making it] an <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive reason). The <s>sapakṣa</s> of sound not produced by effort

body.text: 40. tathā prayatnānantarīyakatve śabdasya sādhye 'nityatvaṃ hetuḥ ghaṭādau sarvatra vidyate / aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ punar vidyudākāśādir vipakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśe vidyudādau vartate nākāśādau / tasmād ayaṃ vipakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ sapakṣavyāpī hetur anaikāntikaḥ //
body.translated_text: 40. Likewise, when 'sound is produced by effort' is the thesis, the reason 'impermanence' is present everywhere in pots and so forth. The <s>vipakṣa</s> of what is not produced by effort is lightning, space, etc. Among those, it occurs in part, namely in lightning and so forth, but not in space and so forth. Therefore, this is a <s>vipakṣaikadeśavṛtti sapakṣavyāpī</s> (inconclusive reason occurring in part of the dissimilar instances and pervading the similar instances).

body.text: 41. ubhayapakṣaikadeśavṛttir anaikāntiko yathā / śabde dharmiṇi nityatve sādhye 'mūrtatvād iti hetuḥ / paramāṇvākāśādiḥ sapakṣo 'sya / tatraikadeśe 'mūrtatvam ākāśe pravartate na paramāṇau mūrtatvāt paramāṇūnam / ghaṭasukhādir anityo vipakṣaḥ / tatraikadeśe sukhādau vidyate na ghaṭādau //
body.translated_text: 41. An example of an <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive reason) occurring in part of both sides: When the subject is sound and 'permanent' is the thesis, the reason is 'because of being formless.' The <s>sapakṣa</s> is atoms, space, etc. Among those, formlessness occurs in space, not in atoms, since atoms are corporeal. The <s>vipakṣa</s> of impermanent [things] is pot, pleasure, etc. Among those, it is found in pleasure and so forth, not in pot and so forth.

body.text: 42. tathā saṃdigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikaḥ sapakṣavyāpī hetur anaikāntiko yathā / kapilādidharmy asarvajña iti sādhye vaktṛtvād iti hetuḥ / rathyāpuruṣādau sapakṣe 'sti / vipakṣe sarvajñe saṃdigdhaḥ / sarvajñasyātīndriyatvād vacanam asti na veti saṃdigdham //
body.translated_text: 42. Likewise, an <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive reason) that pervades the <s>sapakṣa</s> but has doubtful exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s>: When <s>Kapila</s> and so forth is the subject, 'non-omniscient' is the thesis, the reason 'because of being a speaker' is present in the <s>sapakṣa</s> of ordinary persons and so forth, but is doubtful regarding the <s>vipakṣa</s> of the omniscient one; since the omniscient one is beyond the senses, it is doubtful whether speech exists or not.

body.text: 43. tathā saṃdigdhasapakṣavṛttir vipakṣavyāpl hetur anaikāntiko yathā / ṛṣabhavardhāmānādidharmī sarvajña iti sādhye kevaliśāstrakaraṇād iti hetuḥ sapakṣe sarvajñe saṃdigdhaḥ / sarvajñasyātīndriyatvāt kevaliśāstrakaraṇaṃ saṃdigdham / vipakṣe varāhamihirādāv asarvajñe vidyate //
body.translated_text: 43. Likewise, an <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive reason) that pervades the <s>vipakṣa</s> but has doubtful occurrence in the <s>sapakṣa</s>: When <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and so forth is the subject, 'omniscient' is the thesis, the reason 'because of composing authoritative scriptures alone' is doubtful in the <s>sapakṣa</s> of the omniscient one; since the omniscient one is beyond the senses, composing authoritative scriptures alone is doubtful. In the <s>vipakṣa</s> of the non-omniscient, such as <s>Varāhamihira</s> and so forth, it is present.

body.text: 44. saṃdigdhānvayavyatirekahetur anaikāntiko yathā sātmakaṃ jīvaccharīraṃ prāṇādimattvād iti hetuḥ / jīvaccharīrasaṃbandhī prāṇādir na sātmake

children.translated_text: or in what lacks a self,
whether it is present or absent.

body.translated_text: 44. A <s>hetu</s> (reason) with doubtful positive and negative concomitance is <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive). For example, the <s>hetu</s>: 'A living body possesses a self, because of possessing breath and such.' The breath and such, related to a living body, is not ascertained as occurring in what possesses a self

body.text: 45. tataḥ kevalānvayī hetur dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 45. Hence, a purely positive <s>hetu</s> (<s>kevalānvayī</s>) is inconclusive because of the absence of an example.

body.text: 46. tathā dvitīyo 'pi kevalavyatirekī nedaṃ nirātmakaṃ jīvaccharīra

children.text: aprāṇādimattvaprasaṅgād iti / dṛṣṭāntābhāvād eva nānvayaniścayo nāpi vyatirekaniścaya iti saṃśayahetuḥ //
children.translated_text: is not without a self, because of the undesirable consequence of lacking breath and such.' Due to the very absence of an example, there is neither certainty of positive concomitance nor certainty of negative concomitance; hence it is a <s>saṃśayahetu</s> (doubt-producing reason).

body.translated_text: 46. Likewise, the second, purely negative (<s>kevalavyatirekī</s>): 'This living body

body.text: 47. uktā nava ete 'naikāntikasaṃjñakā hetvābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 47. These nine <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (semblances of reason) designated as <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) have been stated.

body.text: 48. viruddhasaṃjñako hetvābhāsaḥ kīdṛśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 48. What is the <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (semblance of reason) designated as <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory) like?

body.text: 49. yathā śabdo dharmī nitya iti sādhyo dharmaḥ kṛtakatvād ākāśādivat / ayaṃ hetur ghaṭādau vipakṣa evāsti na sapakṣe //
body.translated_text: 49. For example: 'Sound, as <s>dharmin</s> (subject), is to be proved as eternal, because of being produced, like space and such.' This <s>hetu</s> exists only in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case) such as a pot, not in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case).

body.text: 50. tathā śabdo dharmī nitya iti sādhye prayatnānantarīyakatvād iti hetur ākāśādau sapakṣe nāsty eva / vipakṣaikadese ghaṭādau vidyate na vidyudādau // etau dvau hetū dharmasvarūpaviparītasādhanau //
body.translated_text: 50. Likewise: 'Sound, as <s>dharmin</s>, is to be proved as eternal, because of being immediately preceded by effort.' This <s>hetu</s> does not exist at all in the <s>sapakṣa</s> such as space. It exists in one part of the <s>vipakṣa</s>, such as a pot, but not in lightning and such. These two <s>hetus</s> establish the opposite of the nature of the <s>dharma</s> (property to be proved).

body.text: 51. dharma

children.text: viparītasādhano yathā / cakṣurādaya iti dharmī parārthā iti sādhyo dharmaḥ saṃghatatvād iti hetuḥ / mañcapīṭhādivad iti sapakṣavacanaṃ / ayaṃ tu hetur yathā cakṣurādīnāṃ pārārthyaṃ sādhayati / tathā saṃghātatvaṃ parasya sādhayati / mañcapīṭhādīnāṃ saṃghātasya devadattādeḥ parasyopakāradarśanāt //
children.translated_text: of the <s>dharma</s>, for example: 'The eyes and such, as <s>dharmin</s> (subject), are for the purpose of another' is the <s>sādhya</s>; 'because of being composite' is the <s>hetu</s>; 'like a bed, seat, and such' is the <s>sapakṣa</s> statement. But this <s>hetu</s>, just as it establishes the purpose-for-another of the eyes and such, so too it establishes the compositeness of the other, because the composite of bed, seat, and such is observed to serve another such as <s>Devadatta</s>.

body.translated_text: 51. Establishing the opposite of a particular

body.text: 52. dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhano yathā pṛthivyādir dharmī buddhimaddhetujanya iti sādhye sāśrayatvād iti hetuḥ / ghaṭādivad iti sapakṣavacanam / ayaṃ hetur yathā buddhimaddhetujanyatvaṃ sādhayati tathā buddhimataḥ kartuḥ sāśrayatvam api sādhayati //
body.translated_text: 52. Establishing the opposite of the nature of the <s>dharmin</s> (subject), for example: 'Earth and such, as <s>dharmin</s>, is to be proved as produced by an intelligent cause, because of having a substratum, like a pot and such' is the <s>sapakṣa</s> statement. This <s>hetu</s>, just as it establishes production by an intelligent cause, so too it establishes that the intelligent maker also has a substratum.

body.text: 53. dharmiviṣeśaviparītasādhano yathā / vaiśeṣikasya mīmāṃsa
body.translated_text: 53. Establishing the opposite of a particular aspect of the <s>dharmin</s>, for example: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s thesis to the <s>Mīmāṃsa</s>-

body.text: ka
body.translated_text: ka

body.text: ṃ praty ātmā dharmī cetayata iti sādhye
body.translated_text: : 'The self (<s>ātman</s>), as <s>dharmin</s>, is conscious' is the <s>sādhya</s>;

body.text: cetanādhiṣṭhānatvād iti hetur ātmano 'cetanasya yathā caitanyaṃ sādhayati / tathā hetur ayam anityatvam api sādhayati / anityatvād vijñānasya //
body.translated_text: 'because of being the substratum of consciousness' is the <s>hetu</s>. Just as this <s>hetu</s> establishes consciousness for the unconscious self, so too it establishes impermanence, because consciousness is impermanent.

body.text: 54. uktāḥ pañcaite viruddhasaṃjñakā hetvābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 54. These five <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (semblances of reason) designated as <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory) have been stated.

body.text: 55. viruddhāvyabhicārī nāma na kaścid dhetudoṣo 'stīti na tasyodāharaṇaṃ yuktam / tatrodāharaṇaṃ / yat sarvadeśāvasthitaiḥ svayaṃ ca svasaṃbandhibhir yugapad abhisaṃbadhyate tat sarvagatam / yathākāśam iti / abhisaṃbadhyate ca sarvadeśāvasthitaiḥ svasaṃbandhibhir yugapat sāmānyam iti pailukasya svabhāvahetuprayogaḥ / / dvitīyo 'pi prayogaḥ paiṭharasya / yad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ yatra nopalabhyate na tatrāsti / tad yathā kvacid avidyamāno ghaṭaḥ / nopalabhyate copalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ sāmānyaṃ vyaktyantarāleṣv iti // anupalambho hetuḥ pūrvoktaś ca svabhāvaḥ parasparaṃ bādhayataḥ / saṃśayajananāt /
body.translated_text: 55. The so-called <s>viruddhāvyabhicārī</s> (contradictory non-deviating) is not any real fault of a <s>hetu</s>, so its illustration is not appropriate. The example therein: 'Whatever is simultaneously connected by its own associates stationed in all places is all-pervading, like space'—thus is the <s>Pailuka</s>'s (Vaiśeṣika's) employment of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature reason). The second employment, by the <s>Paiṭhara</s>: 'What fulfills the conditions of apprehension but is not apprehended somewhere does not exist there, like a pot absent from some place. And the universal, though fulfilling the conditions of apprehension, is not apprehended between individual instances'—this is the <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) reason. The previously stated <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature) reason and this one mutually contradict each other, because they generate doubt.

body.text: 56. na sapakṣād anyo dṛṣṭānto nāma kaścid iti sapakṣa eva sādharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ // tatra dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ kīdṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 56. There is no example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) other than the <s>sapakṣa</s>; thus the <s>sapakṣa</s> itself is the example through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>). Therein, what is the <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s> (semblance of an example) like?

body.text: 57. sādharmyeṇa tāvat /
body.translated_text: 57. Through similarity first:

body.text: 58. nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt karmavat / sādhyavikalaḥ karmaṇo 'nityatvāt //
body.translated_text: 58. 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like <s>karma</s> (action).' This is deficient in the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved), because <s>karma</s> is non-eternal.

body.text: 59. nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt paramāṇuvat / sādhanavikalaḥ paramāṇūnāṃ mūrtatvāt //
body.translated_text: 59. 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like atoms.' This is deficient in the <s>sādhana</s> (reason), because atoms are corporeal.

body.text: 60. nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvād ghaṭavad / sādhyasādhanobhayavikalaḥ //
body.translated_text: 60. 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like a pot.' This is deficient in both <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>.

body.text: 61. tathā saṃdigdhasādhyadharmā dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / kaścit puruṣo dharmī rāgādimān vacanāt / rathyāpuruṣavat /
body.translated_text: 61. Likewise, a <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s> with a doubtful <s>sādhya</s> property: 'A certain person, as <s>dharmin</s>, possesses passion and such, because of speech, like a person on the street.'

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭānte rathyāpuruṣe rāgādimattvaṃ saṃdigdhaḥ paracetovṛttīnāṃ duranvayatvāt //
body.translated_text: Therein, in the example of the person on the street, the possession of passion and such is doubtful, because the mental states of others are difficult to ascertain.

body.text: 62. saṃdigdhasādhanadharmā yathā / kaścit puruṣo maraṇadharma iti sādhye rāgādimattvād iti hetuḥ / rathyāpuruṣe dṛṣṭānte saṃdigdhaḥ / vītarāgo 'pi rāgīva ceṣṭate yataḥ //
body.translated_text: 62. With a doubtful property of the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) — for example: when the <s>sādhya</s> is 'a certain person is subject to death,' the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is 'because of possessing <s>rāga</s> (passion) and so forth.' In the example of a person on the street, it is doubtful, because even one free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>) may behave as if passionate.

body.text: 63. saṃdigdhobhayadharmā dṛṣṭāntābhāso yathā kaścit puruṣo dharmī asarvajña iti sādhye rāgādimattvād iti hetuḥ / rathyāpuruṣe dṛṣṭānte sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ saṃdigdham //
body.translated_text: 63. A fallacious example (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) with both properties doubtful — for example: when the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is 'a certain person,' the <s>sādhya</s> is 'non-omniscient,' the <s>hetu</s> is 'because of possessing passion and so forth.' In the example of a person on the street, both the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> are doubtful.

body.text: 64. ananvayo 'pradarśitānvayo viparītānvayaś ca dṛṣṭānṭābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 64. Non-positive concomitance (<s>ananvaya</s>), unshown positive concomitance (<s>apradarśitānvaya</s>), and inverted positive concomitance (<s>viparītānvaya</s>) are fallacious examples.

body.text: 65. tatrānanvayo yathā / yo vaktā sa rāgādimān rathyāpuruṣavat / vaktṛtvarāgādimattvayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvapratiṣedhāt //
body.translated_text: 65. Therein, non-positive concomitance is as follows: 'Whoever is a speaker possesses passion and so forth, like a person on the street.' Because of the denial of the cause-effect relationship between being a speaker and possessing passion and so forth.

body.text: 66. apradarśitānvayo yathā / anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād iti / atra vidyamāno 'py anvayo vyāptyā na darśita iti / vaktṛdoṣād ayaṃ dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: 66. Unshown positive concomitance is as follows: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced.' Here, even though the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) exists, it is not shown through pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). This fallacious example is due to the fault of the speaker.

body.text: 67. viparītānvayo yathā / yad anityaṃ tat kṛtakaṃ ghaṭādivad ity atrānityatvaṃ sādhyam / sādhyenaiva sādhanaṃ vyāptaṃ kathanīyam / na tu sādhanena vyāptaṃ sādhyaṃ kathyate / atha viparītānvayo dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: 67. Inverted positive concomitance is as follows: 'Whatever is non-eternal is produced, like a pot and such.' Here non-eternality is the <s>sādhya</s>. The pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> by the <s>sādhya</s> should be stated, but instead the pervasion of the <s>sādhya</s> by the <s>sādhana</s> is stated. Thus, inverted positive concomitance is a fallacious example.

body.text: 68. uktā navaite sādharmyeṇa dṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 68. These nine fallacious examples through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) have been stated.

body.text: 69. vaidharmyeṇa dṛṣṭāntābhāsā ucyante /
body.translated_text: 69. The fallacious examples through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>) are now stated.

body.text: 70. sādhyāvyatirekī dṛṣṭāntābhāso yathā / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt paramāṇuvat / atra paramāṇor vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntatvād amūrtatvaṃ sādhanadharmo vyāvṛtto
body.translated_text: 70. A fallacious example lacking exclusion of the <s>sādhya</s> — for example: 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>).' Here, since atoms are the dissimilar example, the <s>sādhana</s> property (incorporeality) is excluded,

body.text: mūrtatvāt paramāṇūnām / nityatvaṃ sādhyadharmo na vyāvṛttaḥ / paramāṇor nityatvāt //
body.translated_text: because atoms are corporeal; but the <s>sādhya</s> property (eternality) is not excluded, because atoms are eternal.

body.text: 71. sādhanāvyatirekl yathā / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvāt karmavat / atra nityatvaṃ sādhyadharmo vyāvṛttaḥ karmaṇo 'nityatvāt / sādhanadharmo na vyāvṛttaḥ karmaṇo 'mūrtatvāt //
body.translated_text: 71. Lacking exclusion of the <s>sādhana</s> — for example: 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like action (<s>karma</s>).' Here, the <s>sādhya</s> property (eternality) is excluded because action is non-eternal; but the <s>sādhana</s> property is not excluded, because action is incorporeal.

body.text: 72. ubhayāvyāvṛtto yathā / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvād ākāśādivat / atrākāśādau vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntāt sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca na vyāvṛttam //
body.translated_text: 72. With non-exclusion of both — for example: 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal, like space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and such.' Here, in the dissimilar example of space and such, neither the <s>sādhya</s> nor the <s>sādhana</s> is excluded.

body.text: 73. tathā saṃdigdhasādhyavyatirekī saṃdigdhasādhanavyatirekī / saṃdigdhobhayavyatirekī ceti /
body.translated_text: 73. Similarly, there are [fallacious examples with] doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhya</s>, doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhana</s>, and doubtful exclusion of both.

body.text: 74. saṃdigdhasādhyavyatireko dṛṣṭāntābhāso yathā / asarvajñāḥ kapilādayaḥ / sarvajñatāliṅgabhūtakevaliśāstrākaraṇād iti / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇam / yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sa jyotirjñānādikam upadiṣṭavān yathā ṛṣabhavardhamānādir iti / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇād ṛṣabhavardhamānāder asarvajñatā nivṛttāna veti saṃdehaḥ //
body.translated_text: 74. A fallacious example with doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhya</s> — for example: '<s>Kapila</s> and others are non-omniscient, because they did not compose a Jain scripture which is the mark of omniscience.' Here the dissimilar example is: 'Whoever is omniscient has taught knowledge of luminaries and such, like <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and others.' Here, from the dissimilar example of <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s> and others, there is doubt whether the non-omniscience is excluded or not.

body.text: 75. saṃdigdhasādhanavyatireko yathā / nātra trayīvidā brāhmaṇena grāhyavacanaḥ kapilakaṇādādiḥ puruṣo rāgādimattvād iti / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇaṃ ye grāhyavacanā na te rāgādimanto yathā gautamādayo dharmaśāstrāṇāṃ praṇetāra iti gautamādibhyo rāgādimattvasya dharmasya vyāvṛttiḥ saṃdigdhā //
body.translated_text: 75. With doubtful exclusion of the <s>sādhana</s> — for example: '<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s> and such persons are not to be trusted by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, because of possessing passion and so forth.' Here the dissimilar example is: 'Those whose words are trustworthy do not possess passion and so forth, like <s>Gautama</s> and other authors of <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>.' The exclusion of the property of possessing passion from <s>Gautama</s> and others is doubtful.

body.text: 76. saṃdigdhobhayavyatirekī yathā / avītarāgāḥ kapilādayaḥ parigrahāgrahayogād iti / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇaṃ yo vītarāgo na tasya parigrahāgrahau saṃbhavataḥ
body.translated_text: 76. With doubtful exclusion of both — for example: '<s>Kapila</s> and others are not free from passion, because of the association with acquisition (<s>parigraha</s>) and retention (<s>āgraha</s>).' Here the dissimilar example is: 'Whoever is free from passion, for him acquisition and retention are not possible,

body.text: yathā ṛṣabhavardhamānāder iti / ṛṣabhāder vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntāt avītarāgatvaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ parigrahāgrahayo
body.translated_text: like <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and others.' From the dissimilar example of <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others, there is doubt whether the <s>sādhya</s> property (not being free from passion) and the <s>sādhana</s> property (association with acquisition and reten-

body.text: ga
body.translated_text: tion)

body.text: ḥ sādhanadharmo vyāvṛtto na veti saṃdehaḥ / apūrvārthalābhaḥ parigrahaḥ / labdhasyāparityāga āgrahaḥ / tau ca dvāv api ṛṣabhādau saṃbhavyete / chatracāmaradundubhīnāṃ parigrahāgrahaśravaṇāt //
body.translated_text: are excluded or not. Acquisition (<s>parigraha</s>) is the obtaining of a previously unacquired object. Retention (<s>āgraha</s>) is the non-relinquishing of what has been obtained. Both of these two are possible in the case of <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others, because we hear of their acquisition and retention of parasols, fly-whisks, and drums.

body.text: 77. avyatireko vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntābhāso 'pradarśitavyatireko viparītavyatirekaś ceti /
body.translated_text: 77. Non-exclusion as a fallacious dissimilar example, unshown exclusion, and inverted exclusion.

body.text: 78. avyatireko yathā / kapiIādir avītarāgo vaktṛtvāt / yatrāvītarāgatvaṃ nāsti na sa vaktā yathopalakhaṇḍa iti / yady upalakhaṇḍād ayaṃ vyāvṛttas tathāpi sarvo vītarāgo vakteti saṃdehaḥ //
body.translated_text: 78. Non-exclusion is as follows: '<s>Kapila</s> and others are not free from passion, because of being speakers. Wherever there is no non-freedom from passion, there is no speaker, like a stone slab.' Even if this [reason] is excluded from a stone slab, there is still the doubt that every one free from passion is a speaker.

body.text: 79. apradarśitavyatireko yathā / anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ākāśādivad iti / paramārthataḥ saṃyag dṛṣṭānto 'py ayaṃ vaktṛdoṣād dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / parārthānumāne vaktur guṇadoṣayor vicāryamāṇatvāt / tathā hi yan nityaṃ tat sarvaṃ niyamenākṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśādir iti vacanena vibhajya vaktrā vyāptipūrvako vyātireko na pradarśita ity apradarśitavyatirekaḥ //
body.translated_text: 79. <s>Apradarśitavyatireka</s> (unshown exclusion) is as follows: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, unlike space and such.' Although in ultimate reality this is a correct example, due to the speaker's fault it is a <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s> (semblance of an example), because in <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others) the merits and faults of the speaker are to be examined. For the speaker should have distinguished by stating: 'Whatever is eternal is all invariably seen to be non-produced, like space and such' — thus demonstrating the exclusion preceded by pervasion. Since the prior exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>) was not demonstrated, this is an 'unshown exclusion.'

body.text: 80. viparītavyatireko yathā / yad akṛtakaṃ tan nityaṃ dṛṣṭam iti / atra sādhananivṛttyā sādhyanivṛttir vyāptā darśayitavyā tena yatra yatra sādhyanivṛttis tatra tatra niyamena sādhananivṛttiḥ sidhyatīti //
body.translated_text: 80. <s>Viparītavyatireka</s> (reversed exclusion) is as follows: 'Whatever is non-produced is seen to be eternal.' Here, by the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans), the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) should be shown as pervaded, so that wherever there is absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, there the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> is invariably established.

body.text: 81. uktā dṛṣṭāntābhāsā aṣṭādaśa //
body.translated_text: 81. Eighteen <s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsas</s> (semblances of examples) have been stated.

body.text: 82. eta eva sarve pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ / vādinā sādhayitum iṣṭam arthaṃ na sādhayantīti sādhanābhāsā
body.translated_text: 82. All these — semblances of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), <s>hetu</s> (reason), and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) — since they do not prove the meaning that the proponent wishes to establish, become <s>sādhanābhāsas</s> (semblances of proof)

body.text: vādino bhavanti / evaṃ ca prativādinā dūṣaṇatvenopanyastā dūṣaṇāni bhavanti / pūrvapakṣavādino 'bhipretārthasiddhipratibandhāt / sādhanasya nyūnatodbhāvanam eva dūṣaṇasya lakṣaṇaṃ vibhajya pṛthag ucyate /
body.translated_text: for the proponent. And thus, when presented by the opponent as refutation, they become <s>dūṣaṇas</s> (refutations), because they obstruct the establishment of the meaning intended by the original proponent. The very demonstration of deficiency in the proof is stated separately, being distinguished as the definition of refutation.

body.text: 83. dūṣaṇābhāsaḥ / etāny eva dūṣaṇāni prativādinoktāni / yadā pūrvapakṣavādī mithyādūṣaṇatvena pratipādayatīti tadā dūṣaṇābhāsā jātaya iti paṭhyante / abhūtadoṣodbhāvanāni mithyottarāṇi jātyuttaraṇīti vacanāt / yāthāduṣṭapakṣe pakṣadoṣodbhāvanaṃ nirdoṣe hetau hetudoṣakhyāpanam / aduṣṭadṛṣṭānte dṛṣṭāntadoṣopādānaṃ dūṣaṇābhāsa iti nyāyāt / J
body.translated_text: 83. <s>Dūṣaṇābhāsa</s> (semblance of refutation): These very refutations stated by the opponent — when the original proponent demonstrates them to be false refutations, then they are read as <s>dūṣaṇābhāsas</s> (semblances of refutation), which are the <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders). This is because of the statement: 'The raising of non-existent faults and false replies are called futile rejoinders.' Raising <s>pakṣa</s>-faults in a faultless thesis, declaring <s>hetu</s>-faults in a faultless reason, and attributing <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>-faults in a faultless example — this constitutes a <s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s> (semblance of refutation) by principle.

body.text: 84. tatra pratijñāhetudāharaṇopanayanigamanāni pañcāvayavaṃ paraiḥ sādhanam ucyate / yathānityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā kṛtakatvād iti hetuḥ / yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvam anityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā ghaṭādīty udāharaṇam / tathā kṛtakaḥ śabda ity upanayaḥ / tasmād anitya iti nigamanam / dṛṣṭānte pratītisamartho hetur dharmiṇy upanīyata ity upanayaḥ / pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanam iti vacanāt / naitad asti / tribhir evāvayavair anvayavyatirekapakṣadharmasaṃjñakaiḥ sādhyārthasiddheḥ //
body.translated_text: 84. Therein, others state that the five-membered proof consists of <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example), <s>upanaya</s> (application), and <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion). For example: 'Sound is non-eternal' is the <s>pratijñā</s>. 'Because of being produced' is the <s>hetu</s>. 'Whatever is produced is all seen to be non-eternal, like a pot and such' is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. 'Likewise, sound is produced' is the <s>upanaya</s>. 'Therefore it is non-eternal' is the <s>nigamana</s>. [They say:] 'The <s>upanaya</s> is the application of the <s>hetu</s>, capable of being understood in the example, to the <s>dharmin</s> (subject). The <s>nigamana</s> is the restatement of the thesis.' This is not so, because the meaning to be proved is established by just three members, called <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), and <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject).

body.text: 85. tathā hi / vādakāle vyāptipūrvaka eva prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ / yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvam anityaṃ dṛstaṃ yathā ghaṭādir iti / sādhyena sādhanasya dṛṣṭānte vyāptikathanam anvaya ucyate //
body.translated_text: 85. For thus, at the time of debate, the formulation must be preceded by pervasion: 'Whatever is produced is all seen to be non-eternal, like a pot and such.' The statement of the pervasion of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) by the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) in the example is called <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance).

body.text: 86. vipakṣe ca sādhyanivṛttyā sādhananivṛttir vyatireka ucyate yathāsaty anityatve na bhavaty eva kṛtakatvaṃ yathākāśādau /
body.translated_text: 86. And in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case), the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> through the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is called <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance): for example, 'In the absence of non-eternality, there is certainly no being-produced, as in space and such.'

body.text: 87. kṛtakaś ca śabda iti pakṣadharmavacanam / pratijñānigamane punaḥ sarvathā na vaktavye //
body.translated_text: 87. 'And sound is produced' is the statement of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject). The <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis) and <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) need not be stated again at all.

body.text: 88. tathā sādharmyavati prayoge 'nvayābhidhānasāmarthyād eva vyatireko 'vagantavya iti na pṛthag ucyate / yathā yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvam anityaṃ draṣṭavyam / yathā ghaṭādiḥ / kṛtakaś ca śabda iti / sādharmyavān prayogaḥ / tathā vaidharmyavati prayoge vyatirekoktisāmarthyād evānvayaḥ pratipanna iti nānvayaḥ punar ucyate / yan nityaṃ tad akṛtakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśādiḥ kṛtakaś ca śabda iti / vaidharmyavān prayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 88. Likewise, in a formulation through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is to be understood by the very force of the statement of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), and so it is not separately stated. For example: 'Whatever is produced is all to be seen as non-eternal, like a pot and such. And sound is produced.' This is a formulation through similarity. Similarly, in a formulation through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) is understood by the very force of the statement of <s>vyatireka</s>, and so <s>anvaya</s> is not stated again: 'Whatever is eternal is seen to be non-produced, like space and such. And sound is produced.' This is a formulation through dissimilarity.

body.text: 89. uktāḥ sādhanābhāsā dūṣanābhasāḥ //
body.translated_text: 89. The <s>sādhanābhāsas</s> (semblances of proof) and <s>dūṣaṇābhāsas</s> (semblances of refutation) have been stated.

body.text: 90. pratyakṣaṃ kīdṛśam / pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntam / pratigatam āśritam akṣaṃ yad vijñānaṃ tat pratyakṣam / pañcendriyāśrayāṇi jñānānīti yāvat / atyādayaḥ krāntādyarthe dvitiyayeti samāsena pratyakṣaśabdo vācyaliṅgaḥ siddhaḥ / pratyakṣo bodhaḥ pratyakṣā buddhiḥ / pratyakṣaṃ jñānam ity upapannaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: 90. What is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) like? <s>Pratyakṣa</s> is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>). That cognition which has approached and depends on the sense faculties (<s>akṣa</s>) is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. That is to say, it is the cognitions based on the five sense organs. By the compound formation where prefixes like 'prati' etc. have the meaning of 'gone toward' etc., with the second case ending, the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> is established as having the gender of its referent. Thus 'direct awareness' (<s>pratyakṣa bodha</s>), 'direct cognition' (<s>pratyakṣā buddhi</s>), and 'direct knowledge' (<s>pratyakṣaṃ jñānam</s>) are all proper.

body.text: 91. cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyākhyāni pañcendriyāṇi tadāśritāni pañca jñānāni pramāṇāni / tadgrāhyā viṣayā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśākhyāḥ prameyāṇi pañcaiva //
body.translated_text: 91. The five sense faculties named eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body — the five cognitions depending on them are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). The objects grasped by them, named form (<s>rūpa</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>), are the five <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge).

body.text: 92. tac ca pratyakṣaṃ nāmajātyādikalpanārahitaṃ nirvikalpakam abhrāntaṃ ca yadi bhavati / tadā pramāṇam ucyate / darśitasyārthasyāvisaṃvādanāt //
body.translated_text: 92. That <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), if it is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) of name, class, and the rest — i.e., non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) — and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>), then it is called a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), because it is non-discordant with the object presented.

body.text: 93. tatra nāmakalpanā / devadatto 'yam iti yad jñānam / jātikalpanā gaur iyam iti jñānam / viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyam
body.translated_text: 93. Therein, conceptual construction of name: the cognition 'this is <s>Devadatta</s>.' Conceptual construction of class: the cognition 'this is a cow.' Conceptual construction of qualifier-qualificand

body.text: iti kalpanā nīlotpalam iti jñānaṃ / anyad api savikaipakaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣābhāsaḥ / bhrāntaṃ cārthe 'pi taimirikasya dvicandrajñānaṃ / śuktikāyāṃ rajatajñānaṃ sthāṇur ayaṃ puruṣo veti jñānam / anyad api jñānaṃ pratyakṣābhāsaḥ pradarśitārthāprāpakatvāt //
body.translated_text: : the cognition 'a blue lotus.' Any other conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>) cognition is also a <s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s> (semblance of direct perception). And erroneous cognition regarding an object, such as the cognition of two moons by one with an eye disease, the cognition of silver in a shell, or the cognition 'this pillar is a person' — any other such cognition is also a <s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>, because it fails to lead to the indicated object.

body.text: 94. tatra trividhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ / vyavahāram apekṣya indriyajñānam / sarvacittacaittānāṃ svarūpasaṃvedanaṃ svasaṃvedanam / bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajaṃ yogijñānaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: 94. Therein, <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) is threefold: with respect to conventional usage, there is sensory cognition (<s>indriyajñāna</s>); the self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) of all consciousness and mental factors regarding their own nature; and yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) born at the culmination of the cultivation of true objects.

body.text: 95. tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇam arthakriyāsamarthaṃ tu svalakṣaṇam ucyate / sāmānyaṃ tu nārthakriyāsamartham /
body.translated_text: 95. Its object is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). That which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) is called a particular. The universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), however, is not capable of causal efficacy.

body.text: 96. tad eva ca pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam / pramāṇam arthapratītirūpaṃ phalaṃ ca tādṛśam eva / na pramāṇaphalayor bhedaḥ kaścid asti //
body.translated_text: 96. That very <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). The <s>pramāṇa</s>, having the form of cognition of the object, is also the result (<s>phala</s>), and it is of the same nature. There is no difference whatsoever between the <s>pramāṇa</s> and its result.

body.text: 97. anumānaṃ dvidhā svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: 97. <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is twofold: for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) and for others (<s>parārtha</s>).

body.text: 98. tatra svārthaṃ tāvat / gṛhīte ca pakṣadharme smṛte ca sādhyasādhanabhāve paścāt pratipattā yathārthaṃ pratipadyate yena tat svārtham anumānam /
body.translated_text: 98. Of these, inference for oneself first: When the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) has been apprehended and the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) has been recalled, thereafter the cognizer understands the object as it is — that is <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself).

body.text: 99. pakṣadharmaś ca trividha eva bhavati / kāryaṃ svabhāvo 'nupalambhaś ceti /
body.translated_text: 99. The <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject) is of three types alone: effect (<s>kārya</s>), essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), and non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>).

body.text: 100. siddhe hi kāryakāraṇabhāve kāryaṃ hetur draṣṭavyaḥ / yathā yatra dhūmas tatrāgniḥ / yathā mahānasādau / asti ceha dhūma iti [ asaty agnau na bhavaty eva dhūmo yathā sajalapradeśe / asti ceha dhūma iti /
body.translated_text: 100. When the causal relation is established, the effect should be regarded as the <s>hetu</s> (reason). For example: 'Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen.' And 'there is smoke here.' [Or:] 'In the absence of fire, there is never smoke, as in a wet place.' And 'there is smoke here.'

body.text: 101. svabhāvahetuḥ / vṛkṣo 'yaṃ śiṃśapātvād iti / pūrvapravartitaśiṃśapāvyavahāravat / asati vṛkṣatve na bhavaty eva śiṃśapātvam / yathā sthaṇḍilapradeśe / atrāpi vyāpyavyāpakabhāve niścite sati vyāpyo hetur draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 101. The essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>): 'This is a tree, because of being a <s>śiṃśapā</s> (Dalbergia sissoo)' — just as the convention of <s>śiṃśapā</s> was previously established. 'In the absence of tree-hood, <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood never exists, as in bare ground.' Here too, when the relation of pervaded and pervader is ascertained, the pervaded should be regarded as the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

body.text: 102. anupalambhahetur yathā / nātra ghaṭa upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdheḥ śaśaviṣāṇādivat / atrāpi dṛṣyānupalambho dṛṣyābhavena vyāpto yadā niścitas tadāyaṃ hetur gamakaḥ //
body.translated_text: 102. The non-apprehension reason (<s>anupalambhahetu</s>), for example: 'There is no pot here, because of the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions for being perceived, like a hare's horn and such.' Here too, when the non-apprehension of the perceptible is ascertained to be pervaded by the non-existence of the perceptible, then this <s>hetu</s> is probative.

body.text: 103. anumānābhāsaḥ kīdṛśaḥ / pūrvavat / śeṣavat / sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ceti paraiḥ kalpitam anumānaṃ sarvam anumānābhāsaḥ // teṣu tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇasya pratibandhābhāvāt [ siddhe saty eva hi kāryakāraṇabhāve vyāpyavyāpakabhāve ca sādhyasādhanabhāvo nānyathā vyabhicārasaṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: 103. What is an <s>anumānābhāsa</s> (semblance of inference) like? That which is imagined by others as inference — namely <s>pūrvavat</s> (from prior), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from remainder), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation) — all of that is <s>anumānābhāsa</s>, because in those, the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) characterized by essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) is absent. For only when the cause-effect relation or the pervaded-pervader relation is established is there the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, not otherwise, due to the possibility of deviation.

body.text: 104. yathā vṛṣṭimān ayaṃ megho gambhīradhvanatvād iti / gambhīradhvanavato 'pi meghasya vṛṣṭivighātasaṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: 104. For example: 'This cloud brings rain, because of having a deep sound' — since even a cloud with a deep sound may have its rain prevented.

body.text: 105. yathopari vṛṣṭo devo nadīpūradarśanāt bandhabhaṅgādināpi nadīpūrasya darśaṇāt //
body.translated_text: 105. For example: 'It has rained above, from seeing the river flood' — since river floods can also be seen from the breaking of a dam and such.

body.text: 106. yathā pakvā ete taṇḍulā ekasthālyantargatatvād dṛṣṭataṇḍulavat //
body.translated_text: 106. For example: 'These grains of rice are cooked, because of being inside the same pot, like the rice observed [to be cooked].'

body.text: 107. pakvāny etāny phalāni ekaśākhaprabandhāt / upayuktaphalavat / atra bhūyo darśane 'pi sādhyasādhanayor vyabhicārasaṃbhava eva //
body.translated_text: 107. 'These fruits are ripe, because of being on the same branch, like the fruit [already] eaten.' Here, even with repeated observation, the possibility of deviation between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> remains.

body.text: 108. yathā yat pārthivaṃ tat sarvaṃ lohalekhyaṃ dṛṣṭam / yathā kāṣṭhādi) / vajram api pārthivaṃ //
body.translated_text: 108. For example: 'Whatever is earthy is all seen to be scratchable by iron, like wood and such.' But diamond too is earthy.

body.text: 109. yaḥ prāṇī sa sarvaḥ sagrīvaḥ / yathā karabhādiḥ kulīro 'pi prāṇī //
body.translated_text: 109. 'Whatever is a living being has a neck, like a camel and such.' But a crab too is a living being.

body.text: 110. yathā yad dravad dravyam ārdrakṛt tad dṛṣṭaṃ yathodakaṃ / pāradam api dravad dravyam iti / evam anye 'py anumānābhāsā draṣṭavyā iti //
body.translated_text: 110. For example: 'Whatever is a liquid substance is seen to cause wetness, like water.' But mercury too is a liquid substance. Thus other <s>anumānābhāsas</s> (semblances of inference) should also be understood.

body.text: hetutattvopadeśaḥ samāptaḥ // kṛtir iyaṃ paṇḍitarājajitāripādānām //
body.translated_text: The <s>Hetutattvopadeśa</s> (Instruction on the Nature of Reasons) is completed. This is the work of the feet of the scholar-king <s>Jitāri</s>.
